_comment: Deliberate defects injected into run_experiment.py, each paired with the test node that MUST fail when the defect is present. A suite nobody has broken on purpose is not evidence; these defects exercise the suite's ability to catch real bugs. Each defect covers `core` (it is in the method core, run_experiment.py). M1-M4 additionally cover `degeneracy` (caught by the paper's own lambda=0==baseline verification gate at lambda=0, where the gate weight is exactly zero so the defect perturbs the loss/grads away from plain cross-entropy); M5 covers `simplex` (caught by the target-sums-to-one invariant of Eq. 3, NOT by the lambda=0 gate, because at lambda=0 the gate weight w=0 makes the doubled p_tilde term inert and the defect invisible to the degeneracy check). M6 covers `stopgrad` via the gate path: it drops the L->t->w->c->z gate-path term (reverting to the DETACHED gradient, dL/dz=(p-t)/B only), which is the standard self-distillation convention the paper does NOT mark and a variant under which Table 1 is reachable (at the default s=0.15; the literal gradient also reaches it for shallow gates) -- the very divergence an adversarial review rejected; at lambda=0 the gate-path term is lam*...=0 so the defect is invisible to the degeneracy gate, but the frozen-p_tilde finite-difference check (which includes the gate path) catches it. M7 covers `stopgrad` via p_tilde: it removes the Eq. (3) stop-grad on p_tilde (adds the d p_tilde/dz chain term, the trivial-solution hazard the paper warns about, paper/paper.md:213-214); at lambda=0 the extra term is w*...=0 so invisible to the degeneracy gate, but the frozen-p_tilde FD check (which omits the p_tilde chain) catches it. tests/test_mutations.py applies each find->replace to a fresh exec'd copy of run_experiment.py and asserts the must_fail invariant is VIOLATED (the test catches it), while the original holds.

mutations.description: Add a tiny constant to the gate weight so it is no longer exactly zero at lambda=0, breaking the no-op=baseline guarantee (w != 0 => t != y).
mutations.replace: w = lam / (1.0 + np.exp(-(c - tau) / s)) + 1e-6     # [B] DEFECT
mutations.invariant: at lambda=0, make_target returns t bitwise equal to the one-hot label Y

mutations.description: Use h>=0 instead of h>0 for the ReLU gradient mask, so units with exactly-zero pre-activation propagate gradient (wrong ReLU derivative). At lambda=0 the grads then differ from the independent cross-entropy routine.
mutations.invariant: at lambda=0, all four parameter gradients are bitwise identical to an independent cross-entropy routine (which uses h>0)

mutations.description: Divide the loss by B*K instead of B, i.e. mean over elements rather than mean over examples (sum over classes). Eq. (4) is -1/B sum_i sum_k; this defect scales the loss by 1/K.
mutations.invariant: at lambda=0, the loss equals the independent cross-entropy loss (-sum(y log p)/B)

mutations.description: Apply temperature T=2 to the logits used for the loss prediction p, so p = softmax(z/2) instead of softmax(z). The paper's Eq. (4) uses the T=1 prediction; T appears only in the target p_tilde. At lambda=0 this makes the loss differ from plain cross-entropy.
mutations.invariant: at lambda=0, the loss and gradients equal independent cross-entropy (which uses the T=1 softmax)

mutations.description: Double the p_tilde contribution to the target so t = (1-w)y + 2w p_tilde, which no longer sums to 1 (it sums to 1+w). This breaks the convex-combination invariant of Eq. (3) -- the target leaves the simplex -- and is caught by the simplex invariant test and by the target_sum_err structural metric in measured.json.
mutations.replace: t = (1.0 - wcol) * Y_onehot + 2.0 * wcol * p_tilde  # DEFECT M5
mutations.invariant: the training target t lies in the probability simplex (sum_k t_ik = 1 for every example i), because t is a convex combination of y and p_tilde (both distributions) with per-example weights

mutations.description: Drop the L->t->w->c->z gate-path term from the literal gradient, reverting to the DETACHED gradient (dL/dz = (p-t)/B only, the whole target treated as constant). This is the standard self-distillation convention the paper does NOT mark on w (Eq. 3 marks stopgrad ONLY on p_tilde) and the variant under which Table 1's 0.9620 IS reachable -- the exact divergence an adversarial review rejected as outcome-determinative. At lambda=0 the gate-path term is lam*...=0 so the defect is INVISIBLE to the degeneracy gate by construction; at lambda=1 the term is active and the analytic dL/dz no longer equals the literal gradient (it omits the gate path). Caught by the frozen-p_tilde finite-difference check (test_gradient_matches_finite_differences, which FDs the loss with p_tilde frozen and w recomputed, i.e. the literal gradient INCLUDING the gate path; the mutated detached analytic diverges by the gate-path magnitude, ~4 on the peaked net).
mutations.find: dz = dz + _gate_path_grad(p, log_p, Y_onehot, p_tilde, lam, tau, s)
mutations.replace: pass  # DEFECT M6: drop the gate-path term -> detached gradient (whole target constant)
mutations.invariant: the paper-LITERAL gradient dL/dz = (p-t)/B + gate-path term (stopgrad ONLY on p_tilde, gate weight w differentiable in z; paper/paper.md:171-214). Dropping the gate path reverts to the detached variant the paper does not state.

mutations.description: Remove the Eq. (3) stop-grad on p_tilde: add the d p_tilde/dz chain term to dL/dz so gradient also flows through p_tilde toward matching it -- the trivial-solution direction the paper explicitly warns about ('without it the target follows the prediction and the objective admits a trivial solution', paper/paper.md:213-214). At lambda=0 the extra term is w*(1/T)*p_tilde*... = 0 (w~lam=0) so the defect is INVISIBLE to the lambda=0 degeneracy gate by construction; at lambda=1 the term is active and the analytic dL/dz no longer equals the literal gradient (it adds the p_tilde chain). Caught by the frozen-p_tilde finite-difference check (test_gradient_matches_finite_differences, which FDs the loss with p_tilde frozen and so omits the p_tilde chain; the mutated no-stopgrad analytic diverges by the p_tilde-chain magnitude, ~2 on the peaked net).
mutations.replace:
_w = lam / (1.0 + np.exp(-(p.max(axis=-1) - tau) / s))           # DEFECT M7: no stop-grad on p_tilde
    _pt = softmax(z / T)
    _hh = np.sum(_pt * log_p, axis=-1)
    dz = (p - t) / B - (1.0 / B) * _w[:, None] * (1.0 / T) * _pt * (log_p - _hh[:, None])
mutations.invariant: dL/dz = (p-t)/B + gate-path term with p_tilde HELD CONSTANT (Eq. 3 stop-grad on p_tilde only; paper/paper.md:198, :213-214). Adding the d p_tilde/dz chain removes the stop-grad the paper marks, admitting the trivial solution.
